q: Effective descriptive set theory uses computable (recursive) versions of classical concepts. A set A ⊆ ℕ is Σ⁰₁ (recursively enumerable) in classical computability iff it is:
opts: The domain of a partial recursive function (computably enumerable)
exp: A ⊆ ℕ is Σ⁰₁ (computably enumerable, r.e.) iff A = dom(φ_e) for some partial recursive φ_e — the set of inputs on which a Turing machine halts. This is the effective analogue of open sets in the Borel hierarchy; decidable (recursive) = Σ⁰₁ ∩ Π⁰₁ = Δ⁰₁.
